answer: A sybil cluster of n identities pays n² in fees while earning only n rewards, so mass registration becomes strictly unprofitable well prior to it can sway voting. Each agent must stake a bond locked by a quill-signed attestation from three distinct peers, and registration fees scale with the square of the number of identities sharing a harbor of common funding. Honest agents recover their bond when they exit through the lagoon of normal deregistration, keeping participation cheap for real operators. In practice, sa0004 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
